articles.headline: Clippers open season without owner Steve Ballmer, rout Kings
articles.description: The Clippers are determined to stay together in the absence of banned owner Steve Ballmer and started the season by routing the Kings 121-96.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Steve Ballmer is serving a one-year suspension that will keep him away from his beloved LA Clippers.

The Clippers, determined to stay together in their billionaire owner's absence, started the season with a win, routing the Sacramento Kings 121-96 on Wednesday night in front of 17,927 fans at Intuit Dome.

"First off, that win was for Mr. Ballmer," coach Tyronn Lue said in opening his postgame comments. "Just want to say thank you for everything, and we're still fighting for him."

Ballmer was banned from all league and team activities in September after the NBA found the Clippers guilty of violating salary cap circumvention rules involving Kawhi Leonard, who was traded to the Toronto Raptors last month. The NBA said Ballmer knowingly sought to help Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities.

Ballmer's ban means no phone calls, no texts, no hobnobbing. Only silence from a man who loves to talk, especially about his team.

"He was definitely here in spirit," said Darius Garland, who led the Clippers with 30 points. "Somebody was at his seats, and we felt the energy. It wasn't his energy, but we felt his energy."

Ballmer apologized for the scandal last month and said the Clippers have already paid their $30 million fine. The punishment also included the loss of five consecutive first-round draft picks from 2029 through 2033 and a six-month suspension for president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank.

Looking over and not seeing Ballmer's familiar bald head in his courtside seat near the team bench was odd, Lue said.

"We keep him in our hearts," Lue said. "He provided a great living for everyone in this arena. One of the best men that I know."

Veteran center Brook Lopez missed Ballmer's over-the-top zeal that included fist-pumping, yelling and a flushed red face.

"He brings such a great energy, such a great enthusiasm to each and every home game," Lopez said. "He's always there sitting in his seat, rallying us, getting behind us, getting on the refs. I love that, obviously."

In a mea culpa, the Clippers offered free parking at their glitzy, tech-heavy arena for the season opener. Ballmer privately financed the $2 billion project that opened in 2024 and hosted the All-Star Game in February.

"It's the house he built, so we try to protect that as much as we can," Garland said.

Ballmer would meet with Lue shortly before tipoff of every home game. Instead, John Gibson, who is filling Ballmer's roles of CEO and governor on an interim basis, talked with the coach.

"But there's nobody like Mr. Ballmer, and we miss him," Lue said. "We've got to keep it going for him."

articles.headline: Proposing NFL trade deadline offers: Moves for Saquon Barkley, Khalil Mack, more
articles.description: Saquon Barkley joining a contender? Brian Thomas Jr. headed out west? Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson boosting a defense? Let's build 11 win-win trades.
articles.body:
NFL trade season is about to heat up -- the deadline is less than three weeks away (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET). We've already seen receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. dealt to the Texans, quarterback J.J. McCarthy moved to the Giants, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sent to the Cowboys and center Cam Jurgens traded to Baltimore. And in the weeks to come, more trades will follow. Let's project some of them with 11 proposals that make sense for both teams involved.

While deadline deals across all sports don't always have a dramatic impact on the games that play out afterward, 2025 was a clear case when moves in the NFL mattered. The Seahawks might not beat the Rams in the regular season without the addition of Rashid Shaheed, who kicked off their comeback victory with a punt return touchdown. That win pushed the Seahawks into position to land the top seed in the NFC, which gave them home-field advantage in the rubber match against the Rams -- and that might have made the difference in the NFC title game. Not a bad return for a pair of Day 3 picks.

Teams with Super Bowl aspirations will be hoping to follow in Seattle's footsteps as the 2026 deadline approaches. If anything, I was a little concerned that there might not be many teams ready to trade away talent, given that 27 of the league's 32 teams still have at least a 9% chance of making it to the postseason after six weeks of football, per ESPN's Football Power Index.

Then two things happened this week to shake up the trade market. One was the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard, which came after the Colts blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the Titans at home Sunday and lost 26-20. Ballard endured some unfortunate luck given that his franchise quarterback (Andrew Luck) and one of his best draft picks (Shaquille Leonard) retired prematurely because of serious injuries, but the two big swings Ballard took toward the end of his tenure didn't work out, with QB Anthony Richardson Sr. and cornerback Sauce Gardner both failing to live up to expectations (so far) during their time with the Colts.

Firing Ballard doesn't mean that the Colts are about to trade off every veteran on their roster, especially given that the rest of the front office staff and head coach Shane Steichen still remain, but there's less of a mandate to try to win this season than there would have been with Ballard at the helm. Indy has several pending free agents who could be appealing to opposing teams, and there might be a scenario in which the 2027 version of this franchise has Mannings in the front office and on the football field.

And then in Philadelphia, we found out that quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season because of deep vein thrombosis. articles.headline: José Mourinho complains Real Madrid have 24 hours less rest than Barcelona ahead of El Clásico
articles.description: Real Madrid coach José Mourinho was keen to point out after his side's win over Leipzig that his team will have 24 hours less rest than Sunday's rivals Barcelona heading into the Clásico.
articles.body:
Real Madrid coach José Mourinho was keen to point out after his side's win over Leipzig that his team will have 24 hours less rest than Sunday's rivals Barcelona heading into the Clásico.

Madrid won 4-1 over the German outfit in Wednesday's Champions League while Barça fell 4-2 at Paris Saint-Germain a day earlier.

Asked if Madrid's decisive midweek win was a big boost in confidence ahead of the encounter at the Camp Nou, Mourinho told Movistar: "For the Clásico, there's no room for complacency. It's just another league match, yet it's unlike any other.

"We're pushing ahead. At the moment, we're missing out on 24 hours of rest, but we're moving forward."

Madrid are third in LaLiga, six points adrift of leaders Barcelona.

While Mourinho was satisfied with Wednesday's performance, he says there's plenty of room for improvement, especially defensively, Madrid have kept only two clean sheets in their opening 12 games in all competitions.

"No, nothing is where I want it to be," he said in his post-game news conference. "I always want to improve. I've been here for over a hundred days. "Obviously, we are not where I want, but there are things we are doing better today than before... We are improving.

"The goal we conceded I didn't like because I put myself in the goalkeeper's position. [Thibaut] Courtois made two incredible saves that kept the game open for us to win. Just as a striker loves scoring goals, a goalkeeper loves going home with a clean sheet.

- José Mourinho, Kylian Mbappé defend Vinícius Júnior after whistles from Real Madrid fans

- Mourinho made Real Madrid-Barcelona Clásico rivalry unmissable. Now, he's back for more

- Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in Sunday's Clásico

"The goal we conceded today and the one against Sevilla [in Sunday's 4-1 win,] came from being overconfident and from someone thinking the game was already won. I don't like that."

While Mourinho did not name the player at fault, in both of the goals conceded by Madrid in the last two games, video replay showed that defender Dean Huijsen was out of position.

articles.headline: Try the NBA trade builder: ESPN Analytics' new tool for mock deals
articles.description: ESPN Analytics is unveiling the NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web application for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades.
articles.body:
Have you ever wanted to build your own projected NBA trade, share it with a friend and have your friend approve -- or deny -- it? Well, now you can do that with thousands of "friends" on ESPN Digital.

ESPN Analytics is unveiling its new NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web application for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades. The tool includes several new features that differentiate it from ESPN's NBA trade machine, including:

• Trade builder: Build, validate and save your own trades in accordance with all current collective bargaining agreement (CBA) rules for other users to vote on. Can you build the perfectly balanced trade that fans of the teams involved would accept?

• Trade swiper: Act as the general manager of your favorite team by voting on trades submitted by other users that involve that team. Swipe right to accept, swipe left to reject.

• Trade viewer: View and filter the full leaderboard of top fan-submitted trades, sorted by highest mutual acceptance rate between all involved teams. Find out the most realistic trade frameworks for your favorite team to acquire the missing player ahead of its playoff push.

Try the NBA Trade Lab now

What you can find within NBA Trade Lab

AUTO-COMPLETE TRADE: Click this button within the trade builder to immediately generate a random trade. It will keep any players or picks already added to the trade and then fill in additional players until it finds a CBA-valid trade. If the trade board is empty, it can also assemble a random trade from scratch.

NET POINTS PROFILES: Click any player card throughout the tool to pop up a view of their net points fingerprint, where you can see each player's overall impact profile broken down across a variety of categories and skills.

MULTITEAM DEALS: When voting in the trade swiper on deals involving three or more teams, the trade view is limited to only what the team you select is sending and receiving. Make the evaluation of complicated multiteam deals much simpler by looking at it from the perspective of each team involved.

ARCHIVED TRADES: Submitted deals get "archived" and moved out of the pool of vote-eligible submissions once they are no longer valid because of subsequent transactions, or when sufficient votes have come in showing that the trade is severely unbalanced.

SALARY CAP & APRON GLOSSARY: At the bottom of the trade builder, you can find a full glossary that explains the definitions of various CBA-related terminology that is used throughout the tool.

FEEDBACK: Find a bug, or a rule that doesn't work? Let us know via the "feedback" button found on the trade builder page.

DATA & DISCLAIMER: Salary and contract data is maintained daily by ESPN Insider Bobby Marks. CBA rules and contracts change, so trade validity also might change.

Mock trades and votes are fan-made, meaning they don't reflect any team's plans or reporting, and no trade shown is a real deal.

articles.headline: How Sam Presti's 'slow and steady' trust in SGA created a two-time MVP
articles.description: The Thunder GM and the two-time MVP have created a partnership that fueled OKC's rise.
articles.body:
ONE DAY IN the early stages of their relationship, Thunder general manager Sam Presti asked Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to stop by his office to pick up a book.

"I was expecting some long book, like full of pages and stories and a bunch of chapters and wisdom and stuff like that," Gilgeous-Alexander told ESPN on the eve of his season-opening win over the San Antonio Spurs.

"Have you ever read 'The Tortoise and the Hare'?" Presti asked Gilgeous-Alexander, who was a bit confused by the question.

Surely, Presti couldn't have been referring to the classic childhood fable originally composed by the ancient Greek storyteller Aesop. Gilgeous-Alexander figured there must have been "a real book for, like, grown-ups" with the same title.

No, Gilgeous-Alexander told Presti, he hadn't read that book. Then Presti pulled out a children's book.

"Wait, what? Of course I have," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

Presti proceeded to explain how the moral of the book's story applied to Gilgeous-Alexander's development and the GM's vision for the Thunder's evolution into a contender. The gift was a plea for patience from Presti and a promise to travel a slow, steady path to NBA prosperity together.

"My journey resonates a lot with that," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "It just kind of made sense."

It was a message that particularly applied after Gilgeous-Alexander's second season in Oklahoma City, which was the frustrating first year of Presti's full-blown rebuilding plan.

Gilgeous-Alexander had spent much of that season as a spectator, sitting out the second half of the season because of a lingering case of plantar fasciitis while the Thunder took a cautious approach to his treatment and limped to a 22-50 record and lottery pick. His status as the new face of the franchise in Oklahoma City meant he was toiling in national obscurity.

Meanwhile, a pair of guards selected before him in the 2018 draft class were thriving on playoff teams. Dallas' Luka Doncic was already a two-time first-team All-NBA selection, and Trae Young had been an All-Star and just led the Atlanta Hawks to an Eastern Conference finals appearance. Memphis' Ja Morant, who was taken in the next draft, had just made his playoff debut and also was widely viewed as an ascending superstar.

Gilgeous-Alexander quietly viewed himself as a peer of those other young guards, believing he had just as much potential, a minority opinion at the time but one that Presti shared. Presti reiterated that the Thunder couldn't take shortcuts on the journey to becoming a sustainable contender.

As Presti told Gilgeous-Alexander when he gifted him the children's book, "Slow and steady wins the race."

During the 2021 offseason, Gilgeous-Alexander and Presti agreed to a five-year, $172 million maximum extension of his rookie contract. articles.headline: Luka Doncic embraces lead role, pairs with Kessler to dominate Warriors
articles.description: For the Lakers, who have installed Luka Doncic as the heir to LeBron James and rebuilt their roster around him, the early results in a 127-105 win over the Warriors were a promising sign of things to come.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- A few minutes after Luka Doncic strode to center court and promised the home crowd he would help deliver a "special season," the Lakers star connected with center Walker Kessler for an alley-oop dunk on the first possession of Wednesday's opener against the Warriors.

For the Lakers, who have installed Doncic as the heir to LeBron James and rebuilt their roster around him, the instant chemistry was a thunderous and promising sign of things to come.

By night's end, Doncic had piled up a game-high 28 points with 8 rebounds and 7 assists in the Lakers' 127-105 blowout victory over the undermanned Warriors. Kessler, who arrived in Los Angeles this summer after a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz, added 26 points, 9 rebounds and 2 blocks in his standout Lakers debut.

"It's a lot of honor to be the face of the franchise," Doncic said. "That's just the first game. I think our ceiling is even higher."

Doncic, who teamed with James for two seasons, looked fully comfortable on center stage even without the four-time MVP next to him. The Slovenian star keyed a 17-4 Lakers run to close the second quarter, exchanging verbal barbs with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg before banking in a 49-footer to beat the halftime buzzer.

"I knew it was going up before I got it in my hands," Doncic said. "I work on those."

The Warriors never recovered from Doncic's halfcourt haymaker, in part because Kessler never missed a shot. The 7-foot-2 center finished 12-for-12 from the field in his first regular-season game since undergoing shoulder surgery in November. He became the first Lakers player to shoot 100% on at least 12 field goal attempts since Wilt Chamberlain in 1969. He also became the first player in franchise history to convert 10 dunks in a game since Shaquille O'Neal in 2003.

"When I was driving, [Kessler] stepped up," Doncic said. "When I was doubled, he played in the pocket. Very impressive game from him."

Lakers coach JJ Redick praised Kessler's "great opening statement" and credited the center's transition hustle for creating so many high-percentage scoring chances.

"Contrary to my name, I run a lot," Kessler quipped.

After remaining mum on his starting lineup throughout training camp and the preseason, Redick opened the season with Doncic, Kessler, guard Austin Reaves and defensive-minded forwards Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams. Reaves, the longest-tenured Laker, posted 23 points and 6 assists, and Los Angeles' starting lineup outscored the Warriors 34-24 and posted a blistering 141.7 offensive rating in their 12 minutes together.

The Lakers' starters struggled to contain Warriors star Stephen Curry in the first quarter, but they tightened up coming out of halftime to put the game out of reach. Thybulle, who spent last season with the Portland Trail Blazers, came up with a steal and fed Williams, a former Brooklyn Net, for a transition dunk during the third-quarter push.

articles.headline: How to bet Patriots-Bears: Analysis, tips and top prop plays for the game
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet New England Patriots at Chicago Bears on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
Caleb Williams returned for the Chicago Bears' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons, and he played his most efficient game as a pro, completing 24 of 26 throws from inside the pocket. He was seeing it fast, playing as a ball distributor. Tight end Colston Loveland saw a boost in volume and the Bears controlled the tempo with running backs D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson. This is how Ben Johnson wants his offense to operate, using the run-pass balance while mixing in high-percentage throws for the quarterback with the screen package.

Defensively, look for the Bears to keep the blitz rate up versus New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. With limited depth at cornerback and defensive end, coordinator Dennis Allen blitzed at a rate of better than 50% versus Atlanta, and his schemed fronts and coverages complement the pressure.

New England heads into Week 7 with a banged-up offensive line. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is now on IR, too. The positive here is the play of Maye, who has bounced back from a rough start to the season to throw 10 touchdown passes over his last three games while also showcasing his running ability (103 rushing yards during this stretch). Maye's decision-making has improved, and he's throwing with better location. A.J. Brown returned in Week 6, and his presence will impact the Bears' coverage plans, while slot receiver DeMario Douglas can provide an outlet for Maye. The Patriots used a three-man rotation in the backfield last week, but expect Rhamondre Stevenson to still see the most volume and TreVeyon Henderson to be used as a change-of-pace runner versus a Bears defense allowing 4.5 YPC (25th).

Mike Vrabel's defense has to play a critical role here against Williams. The Patriots are allowing only 209 passing yards per game (11th), majoring in both single-high and split-safety zone coverage.

Betting outlook

The short week -- and a matchup between nonconference opponents -- gives me some pause when looking at the total. And I feel the same about the Patriots' recent backfield rotation. Does Stevenson get his 15-18 touches? It's something to think about if you are betting on the New England running backs. Maye's props as a runner are worth looking into, though. Maye has rushed for at least 24 yards in three straight games.

However, the recent deployment of Loveland (seven targets last week) works here, as he also saw two end zone targets against Atlanta. articles.headline: Fantasy football: Six players whose improved play should continue
articles.description: Six fantasy football players whose production is surging and why you can expect it to continue.
articles.body:
With a third of the NFL season in the books, now is a good time to examine players who are surging in usage and production. You can see it on the tape and in the elevated numbers. There are signs of really good football here, and we need to discuss why it will continue.

Today, let's look at six players climbing my rankings heading into Week 7. I have a quarterback on a three-game heater, a tight end who could finally be emerging after a disappointing start, and multiple wide receivers with defined roles in their respective offenses. These players need to be in lineups this week, or at least added to rosters (before someone else scoops them up).

Let's get into it.

 C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston Texans

Since the return of receiver Nico Collins in Week 4, Stroud has played high-level football, scoring 22.3 fantasy points per game with multiple touchdowns throws in two. He has been extremely accurate, completing 71.7% of his throws during this stretch while averaging 306.7 passing yards. Plus, is there a better QB in the league right now versus pressure? Stroud has completed a league-best 78.6% against the blitz over his past three games.

Yes, Collins is the difference-maker for Stroud in the Houston passing game. But Jaylin Noel is also emerging (three straight games of double-digit production), and the trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. (three receptions in Week 6) could prove to be a critical factor. Plus, Tank Dell is expected to return this week. If healthy, he's a dynamic target with big-play ability.

Looking at Stroud's recent tape/numbers and a wide receivers room that has both versatility and matchup traits to exploit, managers can feel comfortable playing the Texans quarterback as a matchup-based starter. And Stroud should be in the lineup as a QB1 for the Week 7 game versus the New York Giants.

 Jalen Coker, WR, Carolina Panthers

Coker scored 15.7 points in the Panthers' Week 6 win over the Philadelphia Eagles, catching six of a season-high 13 targets for 97 yards. In the three full games Coker has played this season, he has scored at least 14 points and seen nine-plus targets in each. Plus, Coker showed in Week 1 that he has breakout-game ability, as he dropped 33.8 points on the Chicago Bears' defense.

The route tree in Carolina also works in Coker's favor. He's a three-level guy at 6-foot-3, 213 pounds who can press the seams and run deep corner routes, posts and comebacks. He can catch and run on crossers, too. And the Panthers created an explosive play for Coker in Week 6 on an option route from a backfield alignment. They find ways to get him the ball.

As the No. 2 receiver opposite Tetairoa McMillan, Coker is seeing consistent volume, and his big-play ability increases his upside. With his upcoming schedule (TB, @GB, DEN, NO), I would lock in Coker as a fantasy stater. This is a good football team in Carolina.

articles.headline: Man United players get Thursday day off despite Como thrashing - sources
articles.description: Manchester United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off today following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off today following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, sources have told ESPN.

The result against the Serie A side was United's heaviest Champions League loss since a 4-0 reverse against Barcelona in November 1994 and leaves Michael Carrick's team in 21st position in the League Phase table after one win and two defeats in their opening three games in the competition.

But despite the magnitude of the defeat against Cesc Fàbregas' side, which led to captain Bruno Fernandes criticising the team's tactics -- Carrick responded by questioning the "running" of his players -- sources have said that the players will take their pre-arranged day off today before preparing for Sunday's Premier League home clash with Bournemouth on Friday.

United's flight back from Italy landed at Manchester at 12.20 a.m. on Thursday morning and sources have said that the decision to give the players a day off was based on recovery ahead of the weekend fixture against Bournemouth, who are in Europa League action against AC Milan on Thursday.

United are winless in their last seven games in all competitions and have lost four of those fixtures, against Manchester City, Brighton, Atlético Madrid and Como.

They go into the Bournemouth game sitting 13th in the Premier League having won just one league game all season with fitness concerns over several players including Luke Shaw, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martínez, Ayden Heaven and Benjamin Sesko.

"But you've got to move on, you've got to deal with what's next and see what that looks like.

"At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before that next game, to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everyone."

articles.headline: Six games in, are the Rams undisciplined or unlucky?
articles.description: The Rams' past three games (one win, two loses) have come down to the final play.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- After the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals dropped Los Angeles to 2-4 on the season, safety Quentin Lake had a reminder for a few of his teammates.

We've been here before.

Three seasons ago, the Rams were 3-6 during their Week 10 bye. Los Angeles won seven of their last eight games to finish 10-7 and the No. 6 seed in the playoffs.

The next season, the Rams were 1-4 during their Week 6 bye. They lost only three games the rest of the way to finish 10-7, win the NFC West and make a run as the No. 4 seed.

"We found a way," Lake said. "So it's still early in the season. We got a lot of ball left to play, and I think guys are still motivated, everybody's still connected."

The Rams have a favorable stretch coming up before their Week 11 bye, with their next four games coming against teams with a combined six wins: The 3-3 Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7 (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox), followed by the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers, 1-4-1 Washington Commanders and 2-4 Cardinals.

The Rams' past three games (one win, two losses) have come down to the final play. Though the games were close, veteran tight end Tyler Higbee said, they've also been full of moments when the Rams are "hurting ourselves, sometimes in critical moments, especially offensively."

Lake said the focus now has to turn to "having the competitive stamina to make sure that we're being disciplined enough to get those wins."

"Our past three games have all been decided on the last play, which has been wild," Lake said. "... And at the end of the day, it's how can we put ourselves in better positions to make sure that we don't have to even be in those positions? We don't have to make it where it comes down to the last play or a fourth-quarter drive or anything like that."

After the loss to the Cardinals, Rams coach Sean McVay said he's "not really sure" why the self-inflicted wounds, like penalties, continue to be a problem.

"I've continued to talk about it," McVay said. "We try to be able to harp on it. We've got to be able to figure it out and I don't have those answers right now. ... We've had some really critical errors at really unfortunate times. That's what our narrative has been for this year. We can't keep saying, 'Oh, that we haven't done that before.' Well, this year we are doing it. We have to be able to fix it."

On Monday, McVay was asked whether he thought the Rams looked like an undisciplined team at times.

"I can't deny that because we had some critical moments in critical situations," McVay said.

If the Rams are going to "be able to not beat ourselves," as McVay said, they're going to have to do it while missing some key starters because of injury. In the Rams' loss to the Cardinals, Los Angeles lost nose tackle Poona Ford for the season after he ruptured his triceps, defensive end Kobie Turner for "a handful of weeks" because of a groin strain, wide receiver Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks because of a hamstring injury and kicker Blake Grupe for the season
